text:
lee_ops: Heads up — since ~09:45 we've been seeing internal L4 drops for intra-cluster GPU traffic. internal-lb-01 appears to hairpin rack17 -> rack18 through ToR-A/ToR-B and packets are being dropped; RDMA flows stall. Noticing on prod-rack-17/18. Anyone else?

maria_nguyen: Yep — p99 latency for inference pods rack17->rack18 spiked, tcp retransmits increased. Grafana shows big jump around 09:44.

jonathan_w: tcpdump from a client node: `tcpdump -n host 10.1.17.5 and port 443` shows lots of `SYN` packets with no `SYN/ACK` back, occasional RSTs and some checksum offload warnings in dmesg. Example: `10.1.17.5.34567 > 10.1.18.9.443: Flags [S], seq 0, win 64240, options [mss 1460]` and no response.

lee_ops: Quick inventory: host MTU 9000, ToR ports show `9216` on management console — odd mismatch. Also observed `GRO/GSO` enabled on hosts. We pushed a ToR firmware batch yesterday (rollout-2026-03-16) — could be related.

andre_s: Confirmed firmware 2.4.1 was rolled to ToR-A/B yesterday. We had a couple regressions in test but they passed. If this is the firmware, we should consider rollback.

katie_prod: Rolling back production ToRs will be disruptive. Can we do a host-level workaround first? Try disabling LRO/GRO/GSO on affected nodes: `ethtool -K eth0 gro off gso off lro off` — that often fixes offload-induced checksum/hairpin issues.

maria_nguyen: I just disabled GRO/GSO on one canary inference node in rack17. Result: SYNs now complete, TCP connections established. CPU increased ~6% but latency normalized. Recommend applying as temporary fix to rack17/18 node-pools.

lee_ops: I'll deploy a DaemonSet (nodeSelector rack in [17,18]) to run `ethtool` and restart kube-proxy on those nodes to clear any stale conntrack entries from hairpin flows. Also adding an iptables rule to reduce SNAT hairpin behavior on internal-lb-01 as a stopgap.

sre-bot: Incident created: INC-20260309-0412 — infra-oncall paging.

jonathan_w: ToR-A shows conntrack near capacity: `conntrack -L | wc -l` -> ~240k / 262k (~92%). We're seeing `nf_conntrack` hits and subsequent drops. Hairpin loops + retries are exhausting the table, leading to packet drops.

lee_ops: Temporary increase conntrack on ToR-A/B: `sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=524288` and tune `nf_conntrack_tcp_timeout_established`. We're monitoring for any spike after changes.

andre_s: Good. Long term: freeze firmware rollout and open vendor ticket. Action items: pin internal-lb-01 to avoid cross-rack hairpinning, add preflight checks for offload/MTU parity before ToR firmware push, add conntrack headroom to ToR images.

katie_prod: I'll file the rollback change with runbook and KCI to revert ToR firmware for racks 15-20 if vendor patch isn't available in 48h. Also adding a temporary alert to fire if conntrack > 80%.

maria_nguyen: Post DaemonSet rollout metrics: retransmits down ~85%, p99 tail back to baseline. Leaving GRO/GSO off on these node pools until vendor confirms fix. I'll capture pcaps and open a bug with switch-vendor including `tcpdump -w` and the ToR counters.

lee_ops: Closing loop for now — mitigation applied and incident ticket updated. Follow-up: vendor engagement, rollback plan if needed, add automated MTU/offload parity check in CI for firmware rollouts. Will update INC-20260309-0412 with timelines.
